4. Metus maiorum malorum exprimit preces pro obtinenda incolumitate.

Perinde autem agùt homines malorum agmine circumuenti & attoniti, quemad modum ægroti, qui medicorû opem implorant, morbi autem quo tenentur causas & συμπτώματα dissimulat. Quasi verò medicus prudens, morbi ratione non cognita, medicam manum adhibere soleat.

5. Primùm autem confugiunt ad Numen, idq; seu verum, seu commenticiu. Ita enim divinitús comparata est hominum na-tura, ut supra vires oppressa, ad causam omnipotetem & primam sibi confugiedum intelligat: quod cum facit, semetipsam perasta idololatriæ, & fiduciæ in cæteras creaturas iam deficientis coarguit. Nota est illa narratio Diogenis Laertij de Biante, & ἀθέοις qui in eadem cum ipso navi periclitabantur: Συμπλέων ποτὲ ἀσεβέσι, χειμαζομένης τῆς νεώς, ἐπικαλουμένων τὴν θεὸν: Σιγᾶτε, ἔφη, μὴ ἀκούοντα ὑμᾶς ἐνθάδε πλέοντας.

page.notes: Greek text (Diogenes Laertius, Life of Bias) transcribed from a small, faint print; the accents and several letters in the Greek lines are uncertain and not checked against the source, so treat the Greek as approximate. The word after "quam" and the word "perasta" are doubtful. "dissimulat" and "oppressa" are read from a worn long-s. "omnipotetem" and "confugiedum" are printing errors kept as printed. The bottom "6. Vt" is treated as a catchword.
